reason: Phagocytes are shown clearing debris near the cut, an early part of wound repair.
expectation: The phagocytes will clear debris from the wound.

effect: The wound is cleaned, so I can turn to the signals and vessel involved in repair.
reaction: The result matched the expected cleanup.
reason: The repair signals are pictured directing an effect toward the nearby capillary.
expectation: The signals will prompt a change in the capillary that supports wound repair.

effect: The signals prompted a new vessel branch toward the wound, suggesting it can help supply the repair.
reaction: The connected sprout makes the vessel’s role clearer.
reason: The new capillary branch appears ready to join the cleaned wound and support repair.
expectation: The wound will gain a connected blood supply for repair.

effect: The wound now has named surface and support slots, so I can prepare the tissues to fill them.
reaction: The two slots make the remaining repair work clear.
reason: Fibroblasts and matrix nutrients suggest the materials needed to rebuild the wound's supporting layer.
expectation: The fibroblasts will produce supporting matrix for the wound.

effect: The fibroblasts made new connective tissue, which appears to fit the wound’s support slot.
reaction: The collagen being laid into the damaged dermis makes the tissue’s role clear.
reason: The new connective tissue should support the healing skin.
expectation: The connective tissue will fill the support slot.

effect: The new connective tissue filled the support slot; the surface still needs to close.
reaction: The note that young tissue is not yet as strong makes the repair feel less instantaneous.
reason: The epidermal edge cells need nutrients to grow and close the surface.
expectation: The cells will form new surface tissue for the wound.

effect: The edge cells formed a new surface that appears ready to fill the remaining slot.
reaction: The sheet growing across the gap makes the closure process clear.
reason: The new surface should close the wound over its supporting tissue.
expectation: The new surface will fill the surface slot.

effect: The surface and support are in place; the remaining goal is to clear the temporary clot.
reaction: The reminder that deeper tissue is still gaining strength makes the closure feel like one stage of repair.
reason: The clot-clearing enzymes are described breaking down fibrin, which reinforced the temporary plug.
expectation: The enzymes will break down the temporary clot.

effect: The temporary clot has mostly cleared, while the new tissue and maturing scar remain. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The distinction between clearing the clot and continuing to strengthen the tissue was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the connective tissue was most worthwhile: it connected fibroblasts and collagen to support beneath the wound and explained that young tissue is still weaker.

leastWorthwhile.text: Preparing and then fitting the new surface felt somewhat repetitive, though the picture made clear that cells grow across the gap.

surprise.text: The connected capillary sprout made it clearer that a new vessel branch can grow toward a wound while remaining part of the circulation.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the item descriptions and named slots gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it explored a new relationship with this level of clarity, although the repeated preparation and fitting steps might become predictable.
